anchors.description: Straight top-rail span of the left leaf of the double glass entrance door, between its outer top corner and the corner at the central meeting stile.
anchors.visible_evidence: Both points sit on the same straight white aluminum top rail of the left door leaf, directly under the transom glass; the rail is rigid and planar.
anchors.identity_uncertainty: Leaf widths of German commercial two-leaf entrance doors are typically 985-1085 mm (DIN 18101 nominal sizes); the measured rail segment excludes the two side stiles by roughly 0.1 m, and the exact product is unknown.

anchors.description: Straight top-rail span of the right leaf of the double glass entrance door, between the central-meeting-stile corner and the outer top corner.
anchors.visible_evidence: Both points lie on the same straight white aluminum top rail of the right door leaf, coplanar with the left leaf's rail; the two leaves are closed and equal in width.
anchors.identity_uncertainty: Same DIN 18101 type prior as the left leaf; the rail segment is slightly shorter than the full leaf width because the side stiles are excluded.

anchors.description: Overall width of the two-leaf glass entrance door, taken along the top rails from the outer top-left corner of the left leaf to the top inner corner of the right leaf.
anchors.visible_evidence: The two leaves form one closed double-door unit in a single vertical plane; the straight line between the two top corners runs along the rigid top rails.
anchors.identity_uncertainty: Assumes two equal leaves of about 1.0 m nominal width each plus meeting and outer stiles; custom large-format entrance doors of 2.2-2.4 m total width cannot be excluded.

anchors.description: Outer height of the left door leaf along its left stile, from the top outer corner to the bottom corner at the threshold.
anchors.visible_evidence: Both points lie on the same continuous white outer stile of the left leaf; the top point is the frame corner under the transom and the bottom point is the frame corner at the threshold grating.
anchors.identity_uncertainty: Entrance-door heights in German office buildings range from about 2.1 m to 2.7 m for tall lobby doors; this unit appears tall and slender, and the bottom corner is close to the threshold where depth edges can be noisy.

anchors.description: Diameter chord across the round blue-and-red no-parking sign mounted on the left entrance column.
anchors.visible_evidence: The two points lie on the red annulus of the round sign at almost opposite ends of a near-diameter chord; the sign is a flat printed plate on the column face.
anchors.identity_uncertainty: The sign is the German 'eingeschraenktes Haltverbot' pictogram (single red diagonal); public-road Regelgroesse is 600 mm, but on private property 300-400 mm versions are common, and the sign spans roughly three quarters of the 0.4-0.5 m wide column face, favouring a small format.
